---
title: "Passwords on Start + Void"
description: "Native Passwords runtime, exact-commit qualification, and the held activation and rollback runbook."
---

Passwords (`apps/passwords`) is a TanStack Start app built with Vite+ and the
official Void SDK, hosted as one Cloudflare Worker with a custom entry
(`cloudflare/worker.ts`). It does not resume `apps/tanstack-web`. Its product
and security contract is [Managed Passwords Vault](/platform/features/passwords-vault).

Activation is **held**. `void.config.ts` declares no `routes`, `workers_dev` is
off, and no deploy workflow exists. A merged build is CI-verified, not delivered.

## Request ownership

| Request | Owner and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `/assets/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/site.webmanifest` | `ASSETS` binding (`GET`, `HEAD`). |
| `/api/build-info` | Local build identity. |
| Session endpoints (`verify-app-token`, `refresh-app-session`, `logout`) and unauthenticated page requests | The runtime `edge` from `createPasswordsRuntime`, before Start. |
| `/_passwords/functions/*` | Start server functions. Same-origin CSRF middleware applies to every one. |
| Everything else | Start SSR with the request-bound service from the runtime. |

## Stop fence

`PASSWORDS_ENABLED` is a Worker var whose committed value is `false`. Vault work
runs only when it is exactly the string `true`; a missing, empty or differently
spelled value is disabled. The Worker reads the binding on every invocation, so
the state lives in durable Worker configuration, never in module memory. When it
is disabled the Worker answers every request except static assets and
`/api/build-info` with `503 {"code":"STOPPED"}` before it builds the runtime, so
no session, database, storage or token-exchange call is made. The service handed
to Start is wrapped with the same check, and nothing schedules a retry or a
background job. Hiding controls in the UI is not a stop; the server gate is.

Every non-asset response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-store`,
`X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`
and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. Secret reveals are `POST` server functions, so no
identifier or value appears in a URL.

Domain logic is reached only through the typed port in `src/service/port.ts`.
The single implementation is `src/service/adapter.server.ts`; the app never
reads Supabase, storage or the master key itself.

## Access and recovery

The adapter verifies the signed `passwords` app session using the explicit shared
coordination secret. Each request creates its own service-role client and checks
the actor, workspace membership, deletion, ban and archive state before privileged
RPCs. SQL repeats those checks. This is an explicit request-bound membership
proof; an app-session token is not a Supabase JWT and does not impersonate a
user through RLS.

Step-up starts at the same-origin `/api/auth/step-up?next=<encoded local path>`.
The edge binds a fresh state cookie before redirecting to central MFA challenge
or enrollment. A new assured handoff proves freshness; token refresh does not.

A vault supports at most 16 live file items in this initial release. Browser
uploads are limited to 1 MiB; the agent transport limit is 5 MiB. Rotation is
sequential and commits the complete new encrypted set atomically. Immutable
uploads use no upsert, and the service reads back actual ciphertext bytes before
registration. There are no background retries, object deletions or crons.

Before a browser write, a metadata-only session journal retains its original
request and vault identity. An uncertain result blocks further workspace writes
until a fresh audited status observation confirms the original receipt. A
missing receipt remains unknown. Audited key-read and rotation-snapshot phase
identities also prevent repeating an upload after a process restart. JavaScript
string clearing and clipboard clearing remain best effort.

## Local verification

Run focused checks through the resource queue. Do not run `build:cloudflare`
locally; CI builds the exact commit.

```bash
ttr resources run -- bun --cwd apps/passwords run test
ttr resources run -- bun --cwd apps/passwords run type-check
```

## CI qualification

`passwords-cloudflare.yaml` checks out the exact head SHA, builds the Start SSR
output, rejects route-tree drift, type-checks, discovers the emitted Wrangler
config and asserts the `tuturuuu-passwords` identity with only an `ASSETS`
binding and no triggers, dry-runs Wrangler without publication, then seals and
retains the Worker as `passwords-native-<sha>`. Permissions are read-only, every
action is pinned by SHA, and the workflow has no secrets and no deploy job.

## Names

Names only; values live in the Worker secret store and are never committed.

| Kind | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-passwords` |
| Domain | `passwords.tuturuuu.com` (custom domain, added by the activation change) |
| Binding | `ASSETS` |
| Vars | `PASSWORDS_ENABLED` (committed `false`), `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL` |
| Secrets | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` |
| Central web activation var | `PASSWORDS_APP_URL` (set after the Worker canary passes; enables workspace navigation) |
| App-session target | `passwords` |
| GitHub OIDC audience (machine CLI) | `tuturuuu-passwords` (new). `tuturuuu-mobile-deployment` is unchanged. |

`ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` wraps vault data keys with the same key and AES-256-GCM
envelope as the mobile vault, so both apps share that key's trust boundary.

## Activation

Do not switch traffic without a filled release record.

1. **Release record.** Exact accepted `main` SHA, the green
   `passwords-cloudflare.yaml` run and artifact hash, account and zone IDs,
   operator and rollback owner.
2. **Gates.** User-approved migration summary applied by the gated production
   workflow, independent security review from a different model family, and the
   stop fence tested end to end with the real service (stop, restart, retry and
   operation-count behavior). Rate limits and billing alerts are not a stop.
3. **Secrets file.** Prepare the five named secrets in a private mode-0600 JSON file from the existing store. Reuse the existing master key and shared coordination secret. Once the disabled Worker exists in step 4, upload with `bun x --no-install wrangler secret bulk --config <emitted-config> <private-file>`. Never place a value in arguments, environment variables, logs or the release record.
4. **Publish disabled.** Restore the sealed `passwords-native-<sha>` artifact
   without rebuilding and publish its emitted config with the pinned Wrangler
   adapter (Void rebuilds on its own deploy, so `void deploy` is not used). The
   committed `PASSWORDS_ENABLED=false` applies:

   ```bash
   bun x --no-install wrangler deploy --config <emitted-config> --message "<sha> disabled"
   ```

   The deploy workflow is a separate reviewed change. This page does not
   authorize one.
5. **Domain.** The orchestrator attaches the custom domain in the Tuturuuu
   Cloudflare account: **Workers & Pages → tuturuuu-passwords → Settings →
   Domains & Routes → Add → Custom Domain → passwords.tuturuuu.com**. The record
   is `hostname=passwords.tuturuuu.com`, `service=tuturuuu-passwords`,
   `environment=production`, zone `tuturuuu.com`. Cloudflare manages its DNS and
   certificate. This serves every path on that hostname; no additional
   `passwords.tuturuuu.com/*` route is required. Resolve any existing DNS conflict
   through the owning operator rather than replacing an unrelated record.

   Keep both `route` and `routes` absent from the source and emitted config:
   [Cloudflare supports dashboard-managed routing when they are omitted](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/).
   This attaches the domain without rebuilding or modifying sealed bytes.
   Verify `/api/build-info` reports the accepted SHA and a page returns
   `503 STOPPED` before enabling.
6. **Enable.** Only the operator, and only after the approved migrations,
   reviewed source and exact Worker acceptance are in the release record,
   redeploys the same sealed bytes with the override. A deploy without the
   override restores `false`, and a dashboard edit is overwritten by the next
   deploy, so always state the value in the command and the record:

   ```bash
   bun x --no-install wrangler deploy --config <emitted-config> --var PASSWORDS_ENABLED:true --message "<sha> enabled"
   ```

7. **Canary.** A bounded read and write on a synthetic vault: create, put a
   synthetic file, reveal with fresh MFA, confirm a stale proof is refused,
   confirm each action appears in the audit view, rotate, revoke a member.
   Record operation counts. Then set `PASSWORDS_APP_URL` on central web to the activated origin and publish web to enable its workspace navigation. The navigation entry has no vault authority; every operation still requires current workspace membership and the vault role.

## Rollback

- **Triggers:** any plaintext in a log, response cache or URL; a reveal without
  fresh MFA; a cross-workspace read; sustained 5xx above the agreed threshold.
- **Disable first:** redeploy the same Worker version with the fence closed
  (omit the override, or pass `--var PASSWORDS_ENABLED:false`), then record the
  new version ID:

  ```bash
  bun x --no-install wrangler deploy --config <emitted-config> --var PASSWORDS_ENABLED:false --message "<sha> disabled"
  ```

  Verify with fresh invocations that a page request and a server-function call
  return `503 STOPPED`, and that the vault operation receipts, audit rows and
  storage object counts do not change across the probe. Do not restore code until
  this is recorded.
- **Then restore code:** restore the prior accepted sealed artifact and publish
  its emitted config with the fence explicitly closed:

  ```bash
  bun x --no-install wrangler deploy --config <previous-emitted-config> --var PASSWORDS_ENABLED:false --message "<previous-sha> rollback disabled"
  ```

  Repeat the zero-operation probe before any separately authorized enable.
  Do not use a version rollback that restores an older enabled binding. The
  first deployment has no prior artifact: keep the fence closed and detach the
  custom domain if the operator needs to remove ingress.
- **Data:** rollback never deletes vault rows, ciphertext or audit events.
  Secret changes can block rollback; read the error before bypassing a check.

The rollback command uses the prior sealed artifact's emitted config and the
explicit false override. Do not restore an older enabled configuration through
an unqualified version rollback. Keep the custom domain, encrypted data, key
versions and audit history; database reversal is a separate approved operation.
